title: acre shapes text with rustybuzz and the scene measures it
body:
`render::text_paths` in `crates/acre/src/render.rs` sets each glyph at the advance of the one before, with no kerning, ligatures or contextual forms. The scene cannot measure text at all: `scene::primitive::bounds` guesses 0.6 of the size per character. Every later feature in the milestone needs real widths: wrapping, boxes sized to text, layout, code blocks and math.

## Proposal

- Shape every run with rustybuzz, a pure-Rust port of HarfBuzz, against the embedded fonts. The renderer draws the shaped glyphs at their shaped positions.
- Move the fonts and a shaping function where both `scene` and `render` reach them, for example a `text` module in the `acre` crate, so the scene measures with the same metrics the renderer draws with. `scene` still produces no pixels.
- A measure of a `Label`: its width, its line height, and the ascent and descent of its first and last lines.
- `Scene::bounds` uses the real measure in place of the 0.6 guess.

## Cost

- One new dependency, rustybuzz, which uses `ttf-parser`, already a dependency.
- `Primitive::Text` may hold shaped glyphs in place of strings. That is a change to the library's public types, so it takes a minor version bump.

## Open

- Whether shaping runs once in `scene`, with `Primitive::Text` carrying glyph ids and positions, or again in `render`. Shaping once keeps the two in step.
close_reason: Landed uncommitted on dev: crates/acre/src/text.rs shapes runs with rustybuzz, breaks lines, and places and measures a layout. render draws the shaped glyphs from it, and scene's Label::size and Scene::bounds measure with it. Primitive::Text still carries runs, and render lays them out again from the same function.
